title: Thiou Carry Guinar, Chicken Curry
localName: Thiou carry guinar — curry de poulet à la sénégalaise
author: Aïssatou Mbaye
desc: A Senegalese-style chicken curry built on a vegetable thiou: three tablespoons of Indian curry powder, carrots, potatoes, cabbage and sweet potato in a litre and a half of water.
longDesc: The Aistou Cuisine post is a thiou in disguise — vegetables stewed in tomato and onion — remixed with Indian curry powder. Carrots, potatoes, cabbage, sweet potato, aubergine and a fresh tomato go in a pot with garlic and three generous tablespoons of curry, cook about five minutes, then 1.5 litres of water. Onions go in at the boil. After about 20 minutes the heat is lowered and the pot simmers another 30; halfway through, the chicken is added, and the sweet potato and aubergine are taken out. Rice goes alongside.
ingredients: 3 tbsp Indian curry powder (‘3 belles cuillères à soupe’ in the method)
Salt and pepper — quantities not printed
steps: Peel and wash the vegetables. Cut the carrots into rounds, the potatoes into quarters, the onions into dice and the tomato roughly.
Heat the oil, add the tomato pieces, the curry, salt, pepper and garlic, and cook about 5 minutes, stirring from time to time.
Add the water. When it boils, add the cut onions and the bay leaf.
Stir in the vegetables and cook everything about 20 minutes.
Lower the heat and simmer another 30 minutes.
Halfway through the cooking, add the chicken and remove the sweet potato and the aubergine.
chefTips: The post prints no doneness cue at all: this is a time-driven recipe. Check the chicken is cooked through before serving.
The page’s step says ‘3 belles cuillères à soupe’ of curry while the list says ‘3 c. à soupe’. Start with level tablespoons and add to taste.
Remove the sweet potato and aubergine when the page says; they are done and would otherwise dissolve into the sauce.
Chicken quantity is not printed. Allow roughly 150–200 g per person.
commonMistakes: Adding the chicken at the start so it overcooks.
Leaving the sweet potato and aubergine in until they fall apart.
Under-seasoning — the page prints no salt quantity.
reheating: Gentle heat with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Curry spices add turmeric’s curcumin and other polyphenols.
A high vegetable load gives fibre and vitamin A.
culturalNote: Mbaye’s post says that ‘in Senegal we like to remix dishes and put them in our own sauce’, and that Senegalese paella has become a fixture at Dakar parties. She adds that the curry reminds her of the spice markets of India.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Thiou Carry Guinar (curry de poulet à la sénégalaise)’. Byline: Aïssatou Mbaye (Aistou Cuisine). Date: 17 February 2022. Yield: none printed (6 is an editorial estimate). TWO-PASS on every figure.
CHICKEN QUANTITY ABSENT: chicken appears only in method step 8, with no weight or count. Flagged, not estimated in the ingredients.
Printed oddities: ‘1.5 L’ with a point (against ‘1,5 litre’ elsewhere on her site); the list says ‘3 c. à soupe de curry’ and the method says ‘3 belles cuillères à soupe’. Recorded as printed.
Doneness cues: NONE PRINTED. The recipe is driven purely by elapsed time (about 5 minutes, about 20 minutes, 30 minutes more).
Class A page (ingredient list in the server-rendered HTML). Method step 1 is missing from the page (numbering starts at 2) — a site rendering fault noted across her pages.
The post’s own remark that ‘la paella à la sénégalaise est devenue un inconditionnel des fêtes dakaroises’ is quoted from her cultural note, not from a recipe step.
